jobs.title: Compensation Program Manager
jobs.description:
The Compensation Program Manager plays a critical role in the administration, execution, and continuous improvement of enterprise compensation programs within a highly matrixed organization. Reporting to the Director, Compensation, this role partners closely with HR and Total Rewards Partners, Talent Acquisition, HR Systems, Finance, and business leaders to manage core compensation operations, annual pay planning processes, job architecture activities, and compensation analytics.
This position requires strong operational expertise, analytical capability, and hands-on experience with Workday compensation processes in a large, complex enterprise environment. The ideal candidate brings a balance of strategic thinking and operational execution, with the ability to manage multiple priorities while delivering high-quality client support and scalable compensation solutions.
Responsibilities
Compensation Program Administration
- Administer and support enterprise-wide compensation programs, including annual merit and bonus cycles, promotions, market adjustments, and off-cycle compensation actions

- Partner with HR and Total Rewards Partners and business leaders to provide guidance on compensation decisions, pay positioning, and internal equity considerations

- Support the development, implementation, and administration of salary structures, incentive programs, and compensation policies

- Ensure compensation programs are executed accurately, consistently, and in compliance with company guidelines and regulatory requirements

- Participate in compensation planning activities related to organizational changes, workforce planning, and talent retention initiatives

Job Architecture & Market Pricing
- Support the ongoing maintenance and governance of the company’s job architecture, leveling framework, and career progression structures

- Conduct job evaluations and market pricing analyses using compensation survey data and external benchmarking tools

- Partner with Talent Acquisition and HR teams to develop competitive compensation packages for new hires and internal mobility actions

- Analyze compensation data and trends to identify market movement, compression issues, and pay equity considerations

Workday & Compensation Operations
- Serve as a key functional partner for Workday compensation administration, configuration support, testing, and process execution

- Support annual compensation cycle configuration and validation activities within Workday

- Collaborate with HRIS, Payroll, and Finance teams to ensure data integrity and operational efficiency across compensation processes

- Develop and maintain compensation reports, dashboards, and analytics to support leadership decision-making and program effectiveness

- Identify opportunities for process improvements, automation, and operational scalability

Analytics & Business Partnership
- Conduct complex compensation analyses and provide actionable recommendations to HR and business leaders

- Prepare presentations, reports, and modeling scenarios for compensation reviews and leadership discussions

- Support compensation-related audits, compliance reporting, and regulatory requirements, including pay transparency and pay equity initiatives

- Assist with compensation due diligence and integration support related to mergers, acquisitions, and organizational changes

Collaboration & Stakeholder Support
- Build strong working relationships across HR, Finance, Talent Acquisition, and business leadership teams

- Deliver responsive, high-quality consultation and support in a fast-paced, highly collaborative environment

- Communicate compensation programs and processes clearly to managers and employees

- Contribute to a culture of operational excellence, continuous improvement, and strong customer service within the Compensation function

Qualifications
Required Experience
- BA degree and 8-12 years in Human Resources, Business Administration, Finance, Economics, or related field  or equivalent work experience, or Masters with 6-10 years of prior relevant experience

- Progressive compensation experience supporting broad-based compensation programs in large, complex organizations

- Hands-on experience managing compensation processes within Workday

- Experience supporting annual compensation planning cycles, market pricing, and salary administration

- Strong technical and analytical skills with the ability to translate complex compensation data into clear, compelling insights for business leaders

- Experience working effectively in highly matrixed environments with multiple stakeholders and competing priorities

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities
- Strong understanding of core compensation principles, market pricing methodologies, and compensation program administration

- Advanced Excel and data analysis skills, including modeling and reporting capabilities

- Ability to manage sensitive and confidential information with professionalism and discretion

- Strong organizational skills with high attention to detail and operational accuracy

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to present complex information clearly

- Ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution and operational support

- Strong collaboration and relationship-building skills across all organizational levels

Preferred Qualifications
- Certified Compensation Professional (CCP) designation or progress toward certification

- Experience within government contracting, defense, aerospace, engineering, or similarly regulated industries

- Familiarity with compensation survey platforms and reporting tools

- Experience supporting pay equity analyses and compliance initiatives

- Exposure to job architecture design and organizational effectiveness initiatives

jobs.description:
About Leidos
Leidos is a FORTUNE 500® company bringing a mix of innovative technology and sector expertise to customers in the national security, engineering, and health industries. We deliver innovative solutions through the efforts of our diverse and talented people who are dedicated to our customers' success. Guided by our Mission, Vision, and Values, Leidos empowers its teams, contributes to its communities, and operates sustainably—always with a commitment to doing the right thing for our customers, our people, and our community.
The Leidos Intelligence Sector combines technology-enabled services and mission software capabilities in the areas of cyber, logistics, security operations, and decision analytics to support Intelligence Community customers as they address evolving national security challenges.

About the Opportunity
Leidos is seeking an experienced Program Manager to lead execution of a complex, mission-critical Government program. In this role, you will provide strategic leadership for contract execution, customer engagement, technical performance, and operational excellence while ensuring successful delivery of cost, schedule, and performance objectives. As the primary interface between Leidos and Government leadership, you will guide multidisciplinary teams, foster collaboration, and help deliver innovative capabilities that directly support national security missions.

Why This Role Matters
Success in this role requires more than effective program management—it requires trusted leadership. You will shape program strategy, build strong customer relationships, lead highly skilled technical teams, and ensure disciplined execution across every aspect of contract performance. Your leadership will directly influence mission success by balancing operational excellence, sound financial stewardship, risk management, and customer satisfaction while delivering critical capabilities to the Intelligence Community.

What You’ll Do
Program Leadership
- Lead all aspects of contract execution to achieve cost, schedule, technical, and performance objectives.

- Serve as the primary point of contact for the Government Contracting Officer (CO), Contracting Officer's Representative (COR), Government Program Manager, and Leidos leadership.

- Foster collaboration across multidisciplinary teams, subcontractors, and vendor partners to ensure integrated program execution.

- Communicate program status, technical progress, risks, issues, and recommended solutions to Government stakeholders in a timely and transparent manner.

- Prepare and present executive briefings, technical documentation, and Government-facing reports.

Financial & Contract Management

- Lead cost, schedule, and performance management activities, including Earned Value Management (EVM), Estimate to Complete (ETC), funds execution, and financial reporting.

- Review and approve financial, technical, and programmatic deliverables prior to Government submission.

- Develop, maintain, and recommend Integrated Program Baselines (IPBs) and resource-loaded schedules that support effective program execution.

- Monitor contract performance and implement corrective actions to maintain program objectives.

Workforce Leadership
- Lead workforce planning, recruitment, onboarding, training, and retention efforts to ensure continuity of operations and sustained program performance.

- Mentor and develop program personnel while promoting accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

- Coordinate contractor and subcontractor activities across multiple workstreams to achieve customer objectives.

Risk, Compliance & Acquisition Support
- Lead program risk management activities by identifying risks, implementing mitigation strategies, and communicating risk posture to Government stakeholders.

- Ensure compliance with FAR, DFARS, DoD 5000-series guidance, ICD 801 policies, and all contractual and administrative requirements.

- Coordinate Engineering Change Proposals (ECPs), value engineering initiatives, Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) reviews, Award Fee activities, and other customer-directed program reviews.

- Support Government acquisition activities by contributing to statutory acquisition reports, Congressional Questions for the Record (QFRs), and related acquisition documentation.

- Maintain the Electronic Contractor Position Roster Log (eCPRL) in accordance with Government security requirements.

Required Qualifications
Clearance
- TS/SCI with Polygraph, at time of Application, to be considered for the position.

- Demonstrated experience conducting requirements analysis, resource allocation, project costing, deliverable tracking, schedule management, financial monitoring, and executive reporting.

- Minimum of one (1) year of experience managing funds and resources using Earned Value Management (EVM) or other complex financial reporting methodologies.

- Demonstrated experience managing multi-task contracts, subcontractors, and multi-vendor environments.

- Demonstrated experience leading program risk management, quality assurance, and cross-functional technical teams.Knowledge of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS), DoD 5000-series guidance, and ICD 801 policies.

Certifications
Must possess one of the following:
- Project Management Professional (PMP)

- FAC-P/PM Mid-Level Certification

- Defense Acquisition Workforce Improvement Act (DAWIA) Level II Program Management Certification

Preferred Qualifications
- Experience supporting Intelligence Community or other national security missions.

- Experience managing completion-based or performance-based contracts or task orders.

- Experience preparing executive briefings and Government-facing technical documentation.

- Demonstrated ability to build high-performing teams and foster a culture of collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Airport Screening Operations
jobs.description:
Leidos is seeking a Program Manager for Airport Screening Operations to lead execution of a TSA Screening Partnership Program (SPP) task order providing airport security screening services at Frederick Douglass Greater Rochester International Airport (ROC). The Program Manager serves as the primary point of contact for all coordination and communication with the TSA Contracting Officer (CO) and Federal Security Director (FSD) or designee, and holds overall responsibility for screening operations, staffing, compliance, quality, and subcontractor management under the task order.

Leidos' Homeland Sector's Airports, Borders, and Security (ABS) business area delivers air travel modernization, border protection, and critical infrastructure security solutions that help build a safer, more resilient homeland. Operating globally across aviation security, passenger screening, cybersecurity, and border and port security, ABS integrates next-generation technologies to secure the movement of people and goods worldwide.

*This position is eligible for relocation assistance

Primary Responsibilities:
- Serve as the primary point of contact for all coordination and communication with the CO and/or FSD or designee at ROC.
- Be available 24 hours a day, every day, to receive and implement orders or special instructions from the CO, COR, and/or FSD or designee within the scope of the contract concerning matters affecting the operation, protection, or screening of assigned areas.
- Manage the total work associated with providing security screening services, meeting TSA's performance objectives for program management, workforce management, equipment maintenance and materials management, reporting, responsiveness, customer service, quality control, subcontractor management, and safety/health compliance.
- Provide overall leadership for aviation security screening operations, ensuring compliance with contract requirements, TSA regulations, and federal aviation security standards.
- Direct day-to-day management of screening operations, staffing levels, scheduling, and shift flexibility across passenger and baggage checkpoints.
- Own the Operational Summary Plan and Report and weekly actuals reporting, briefing the FSD or designee on strategy-vs-execution differences within required timeframes.
- Monitor and report program performance against the Contractor Performance Management Plan (CPMP) and Acceptable Quality Levels (AQLs); respond to Contractor Improvement Reports (CIRs) and submit Corrective Action Plans (CAPs) as needed.
- Establish and oversee the Contractor's pre-employment, reasonable suspicion, random, and post-accident drug and alcohol testing program for all screening personnel, consistent with 14 CFR Part 120 and 49 CFR Part 40.
- Direct the organizational structure for the task order, including management of subcontractor personnel/roles and the overall quality control/quality assurance approach for screening operations.
- Own compliance oversight for the task order's Information Technology Acquisition Review requirements (RMF/ATO, continuous monitoring, incident reporting, PIV/HSPD-12, staff training/NDA tracking), SSI safeguarding, and the Continuity of Operations (COOP) Plan and annual COOP exercise, or delegate to named leads.

- Coordinate implementation of TSA best practices adopted for ROC (non-uniformed supervisor role, in-queue monitor, Dual-Function Screening staffing, weekly ops readiness meetings, Local Evaluation Testing participation).

- 7 years of general management experience, OR at least 3 years as a certified Supervisory Transportation Security Officer (STSO) or higher position.
- Bachelor's degree in Business, Aviation Management, Public Administration, Security Management, or a related discipline preferred; 4 years of directly related experience is acceptable in lieu of degree.
- Any ONE of the following: - (a) formal certification in program/project management issued by the Federal Government (e.g., FAC-PM, DAWIA, U.S. DHS) or a non-government credential such as PMP; OR
- (b) at least 5 years of management experience in aviation security, airport operations, or personnel security services (demonstrated supervisory experience in a Federal Government environment is highly desired).

- Ability to communicate verbally and in writing in an effective, efficient, and professional manner.
- Must be able to obtain and maintain a Secret security clearance; TSA will sponsor the Facility/Personnel Security Clearance process.
- U.S. citizenship required (a Secret clearance requires U.S. citizenship as a matter of federal policy).
- Strong understanding of federal contract compliance, performance-based contracts (FFP), and operational metrics/CPMP-style measurement.
- Excellent written/oral communication skills, with demonstrated experience briefing senior government customers (CO/FSD-level).
- Ability to work flexible hours, including early/late coverage and 24/7 on-call availability, given ROC's extended screening hours

- Experience supporting TSA, DHS, FAA, or other federal aviation/homeland security programs.
- Experience leading large operational transitions or workforce mobilizations.
- Experience with DHS 4300A/NIST 800-53 compliance environments or comparable federal IT/cyber compliance oversight.
- Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or equivalent.
- Experience with workforce management systems, operational reporting tools, and performance dashboards.

- Secret security clearance required. Clearance must be maintained throughout the life of the contract - loss of, or inability to obtain, clearance may result in removal from the contract.

jobs.title: Deputy Logistics and Inventory Operations Manager
jobs.description:
The Leidos Digital Sector has a unique and exciting opportunity to offer we are seeking a Deputy Logistics and Inventory Operations Manager , who would like to expand their knowledge and grow with the Leidos team on the (AFNCR ITS) Air Force National Capital Region IT Services Program at Joint Base Bolling, MD.

The Leidos Digital Sector is focused on digital modernization services such as enterprise IT solutions, cloud migrations, cybersecurity, analytics, SecDevOps, digital experience monitoring, and AI-enabled operations.

The AFNCR IT Services program provides support services for information systems for Headquarters Air Force (HAF), Air Force District of Washington (AFDW), Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD), Joint Chiefs of Staff, and other Air Force activities within the AFNCR, missions to include the Pentagon, Joint Base Andrews (JBA), Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling (JBAB), and other locations, leased spaces, and alternate sites. The major support areas required are IT Operations and Maintenance; Plans, Projects, and Engineering (PP&E); and National Military Command Center (NMCC). The senior leaders and national defense missions that are supported require that the AFNCR operations never fail, resulting in a fast-paced, challenging, but also rewarding environment.

If this sounds like the kind of environment where you can thrive, keep reading!

The selected candidate will assists in leading end-to-end supply chain, asset management, and warehouse operations across the Air Force National Capital Region Information Technology Services (AFNCR ITS) enterprise. In this role, you will oversee IT hardware lifecycle tracking, ensure accountability and DoD/Air Force compliance for all accountable property, and coordinate daily logistics support across multi-site mission facilities.
